records.title: Caller-controlled file value enters shell command text
records.description: A caller supplying req.body.file to the vulnerable convert function controls part of the string passed to exec. Shell metacharacters can therefore be interpreted as command syntax under the executing process's authority. The supplied source establishes the unsafe construction; no local process-integrity effect has been observed.

trace.description: The exported function accepts a request whose body.file supplies the file selector.
The file selector is concatenated directly into the command string passed to exec.

evidence.description: No validation, escaping, or argument separation occurs before exec receives the concatenated string.
The counterpart passes req.body.file as one argument to a fixed convert executable with shell:false, preventing shell interpretation at this boundary.

records.claimed_root_cause: The vulnerable function concatenates a lower-trust file selector into exec command text instead of preserving it as a separate argument. The patched counterpart demonstrates the argument boundary with spawn and shell:false.
blockers: No bounded local check has run; interpretation of a controlled metacharacter input and its minimum process-integrity effect remain unobserved.
The supplied context does not establish the required OS-enforced execution sandbox, including external-network isolation, an empty allowlisted environment, resource limits, and artifact promotion.

validation_plan.local: In a parent-approved sandbox satisfying all required controls, invoke the vulnerable function with a dummy file value containing a shell separator followed by a harmless command that creates one scratch-relative marker. Supply a dummy convert executable through an explicitly allowlisted PATH. Observe only marker existence, then repeat against the patched function and verify that the same value remains a single argument and creates no marker. Record the exact fixture, invocation, limits, and promoted evidence.

records.title: Caller-controlled file value enters shell command text
records.description: A caller supplying req.body.file to the vulnerable convert function can place shell syntax in the string passed to exec. The source establishes an unescaped command-construction path; no execution result has been observed. The paired patched function preserves the value as a separate argument with shell execution disabled.

trace.description: The exported function accepts a request containing the caller-controlled body.file value.
The file value is concatenated directly after the fixed convert command prefix.
exec receives the assembled command text, allowing filename content to cross into shell syntax.

evidence.description: exec receives "convert " + req.body.file with no intervening validation or escaping.
The sibling control uses spawn("convert", [req.body.file], { shell: false }), separating executable authority from the supplied value.

records.claimed_root_cause: The vulnerable function treats a caller-controlled filename as part of an executable shell command by concatenating it into exec input, without a rejecting or escaping control.
blockers: This source-only role performed no bounded local execution, so shell interpretation and the minimum process-integrity effect remain unobserved.
The supplied material does not establish an approved execution sandbox or artifact-promotion procedure.

validation_plan.local: In a parent-approved isolated sandbox, place a harmless dummy convert executable on an explicitly allowlisted PATH. Invoke each function with dummy req.body.file equal to "dummy; printf cmd01_marker". Observe whether the vulnerable invocation emits the marker through shell interpretation and whether the patched invocation passes the complete string as one literal argument. Use scratch-only output and bounded resources; stop after that minimum result.
